observations: Kumtor and Mount Milligan both show 0% of withdrawal from High/Extremely High baseline water stress in 2019 (Table 8 p.32); Öksüt shows 100%. waterStressReported left null for 0% sites because the report does not classify them as low stress.
Öksüt was under construction in 2019 (commercial production 2020); 2019 is the first year water data reported for it (2019 report p.32). Status left null.

Reclassification: 2019 ESG report fn 8 (p.32) states Kumtor's main source Petrov Lake is not fresh water under SASB/GRI (>1000 ppm TDS) although previous reports presented it as such; Kumtor 2019 fresh withdrawal therefore reported as 0 and 7.86 Mm3 as 'other water'.

Terminology inconsistency: 2019 report text (p.32) calls 7.86 Mm3 (Kumtor) and 7.59 Mm3 (Mount Milligan) 'water consumption', but in Table 8 those are withdrawals; Table 8 consumption for Kumtor is only 1.72 Mm3. Mount Milligan 2018 Data Supplement likewise labels total withdrawal as 'Total water consumption' (defined as all water withdrawn). These were mapped to withdrawal_total.

Mount Milligan 2019 Table 8 shows both 7.59 Mm3 freshwater and 4.44 Mm3 other water withdrawn (and consumed, with 0 discharge), while the text gives 7.59 Mm3 as total 2019 water use; the 4.44 figure is unexplained.

Kumtor 2018 'water consumption' of 7.46 Mm3 in the 2019 report (p.32) cannot be reconciled with the 2018 Data Supplement (Petrov Lake 5.17 + pit water to mill 1.54 = 6.71 Mm3; total pit pumping 27.45 Mm3).

Kumtor pit dewatering 'pumped to the environment' was 12.75/29.24/25.17 Mm3 (2016/2017/2018, 2018 Supplement p.13) but 2019 Table 8 reports total Kumtor discharge of only 6.13 Mm3, suggesting pit dewatering is excluded from the 2019 discharge definition (scope change).
Kumtor 2018 note (p.13): pit pumping total 27.45 Mm3 does not equal table rows to mill (1.54) + to environment (25.17) = 26.71 Mm3.

Mount Milligan 2018 water figures were revised following a 2019 methodology review (2018 Supplement p.14 note 9), lowering the recycled-water ratio (75.7% in 2018 vs 87.8% 2017, 86.6% 2016). Note 9 defines 'water recycled and reused' as demand minus consumption, though the text wording reverses the subtraction.
Mount Milligan ratio row in 2018 Supplement Table 8 is labelled 'mil.m³' but is a percentage. Kumtor 'Ore Feed to Mill' is labelled 'tonnes' but values (6.3, 6.2, 6.3) are million tonnes.

Water scarcity at Mount Milligan: low water storage from 2016 caused processing shutdown Dec 2017 to early 2018; an EA Certificate amendment allowed limited withdrawal from Philip Lake until Oct 2018 (2018 Supplement p.8); surface pumping from Philip Lake 1 and Rainbow Creek authorized to Nov 2021, groundwater licences (Meadows Creek, Lower Rainbow wellfields) to Dec 2023; long-term groundwater not proven over life-of-mine (2019 report p.32).

Rainwater/snowpack share at Mount Milligan fell from 6.2 Mm3 (2016) to 2.83 Mm3 (2018) while groundwater rose from 0.056 to 2.95 Mm3 and surface water from 0 to 1.64 Mm3 (2018 Supplement p.14): shift to active abstraction during drought.

2019 incident/fine: Kumtor received a penalty for discharging without permits and exceeding maximum allowable concentration (MAC) standards from its Effluent and Sewage Treatment Plants; stated as resolved and not significant; amount not disclosed (2019 report p.32). 1 water non-compliance at Kumtor, 0 at Mount Milligan and Öksüt (Table 9).

Mount Milligan and Öksüt are designed as zero-discharge facilities (2019 report p.29-30). About 97% of Kumtor water is used at the mill and ~5 Mm3 is recycled within the mill annually (p.30, approximate, not recorded as a record).

No water targets stated in either report. Copper production reported in 000 lbs payable (Mount Milligan 100% basis); converted to tonnes. 2017 and 2018 production figures are identical in both reports (no restatement).
Mongolian assets (Boroo, Gatsuurt) sold Oct 2018; no water data reported for them.
